value.rationale: A naturally parameterized complex-symmetric linear solve displays a sharp conflict: the unique angle giving the fastest unrelaxed eigenvalue rate causes the worst Euclidean one-step error, with a quantified stiffness-sensitive alignment window. Positive relaxation changes the transient to all finite horizons and moves its peak by an explicit index rule, so the result is a useful diagnostic for stopping a convergent splitting solver after finitely many iterations rather than a renaming or arbitrary table entry.
